title.en: Towers of Hanoi and its optimal move bound

summary: Let a viewer play the puzzle while the known minimum move count stays visible as a target rather than a decoration.
objective: Build a Towers of Hanoi where my move count is compared with the minimum for that disc count and illegal placements are refused.
intent_signals: Let me solve Towers of Hanoi and compare my moves with the minimum.
Show the recursive strategy for the disc puzzle in 3D.
example_prompts: Build a Towers of Hanoi puzzle with legal move enforcement and a comparison against the optimal count.
Show the recursive solution being replayed move by move.
negative_signals: Not a general puzzle solver; the optimal strategy here is the known recursive one for three pegs.
Not a physics toy: discs do not topple, bounce or collide.
not_for: Not a general puzzle solver; the optimal strategy here is the known recursive one for three pegs.
Not a physics toy: discs do not topple, bounce or collide.

entities.name: Discs and pegs
entities.guidance: Model discs with clearly ordered radii and pegs with a visible stack height, so an illegal placement would be obvious even without the rule check.

entities.name: Rule enforcement
entities.guidance: Refuse a move that places a larger disc on a smaller one and say why, rather than allowing it and marking it red.

entities.name: Move ledger
entities.guidance: Show the move count, the minimum for the current disc count and the difference, updating on every committed move.

state_contract.model: Three pegs holding ordered disc stacks, a legal move test, a move counter and the computed minimum of 2 to the power n minus 1 for n discs. Replay of the recursive solution is a separate stored sequence.
state_contract.authority: The stack state is authoritative and rules are enforced before any animation begins, so an animated move always corresponds to a legal committed move.
actions: Pick up the top disc of a peg and drop it on another.
Change the disc count and reset.

invariants: Only the top disc of a peg can be moved, and it may never land on a smaller disc.

The optimal replay applies to a complete source tower, so replay first rebases to that configuration; from there it finishes in exactly 2 to the power n minus 1 moves. An interrupted replay is reported as interrupted rather than as a completed count.
Undo restores both the stacks and the move counter.
A drop back onto the source peg is a no-op that does not increment the counter, and input is ignored while a move animation is in flight.
motion_guidance: Animate a move as lift, travel and place so the disc never passes through a peg or another disc.
Keep the optimal replay steppable; a continuous animation cannot be counted.
known_limits: The bound cited is for the classical three-peg problem; adding pegs changes it and is out of scope.
Illegal moves are prevented, so the scene does not teach recovery from an invalid state.
The stored optimal sequence grows exponentially, so the disc count is bounded by a declared maximum.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: The recursive solution moves the top n minus one discs aside, moves the largest disc and then moves the rest back, taking 2 to the power n minus 1 moves for n discs.

source_refs.locator: Section 2.3 Recursion, Towers of Hanoi move count

object_craft.structure: Discs as chamfered rings with clearly stepped radii and pegs as tapered posts with a base plate.
object_craft.material: Ordered material ramp by size so the size order is readable even in monochrome; base plate matte to avoid competing highlights.
object_craft.articulation: A held disc is parented to a carry transform and reparented to the target peg only after the move commits.

object_craft.structure: A physical counter board beside the pegs showing moves used, the minimum and the difference.
object_craft.material: Opaque plate with high-contrast numerals so the count is readable from the play camera.
object_craft.articulation: Updates on commit and on undo.

physical_contract.scope: Discrete legal-move puzzle with animated carries; no contact physics or gravity.
checks: Illegal drops are refused before any state change.
Optimal replay completes in the stated number of moves.
